edition.name: Migne PL 4 (1844), Ep. LXIV, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Lapsi vero magnitudinem delicti sui cognoscentes, a deprecando Domino non recedant, nec Ecclesiam catholicam, quae una et sola est a Domino constituta, derelinquant; sed, satisfactionibus immorantes et Domini misericordiam deprecantes, ad Ecclesiam pulsent, ut recipi illic possint ubi fuerunt, et ad Christum redeant, a quo recesserunt. Nec audiant eos qui se fallaci et mortali seductione decipiunt, cum scriptum sit: Nemo vos decipiat inanibus verbis. Propterea enim venit ira Dei super filios contumaciae. Nolite ergo esse participes eorum. Ergo contumaces et Deum non timentes et ab Ecclesia in totum recedentes nemo comitetur. Quod si quis impatiens fuerit ad deprecandum Dominum qui offensus est, et nobis obtemperare noluerit, sed desperatos et perditos secutus fuerit, sibi imputabit cum judicii dies venerit. Quomodo enim deprecari in die illo Dominum poterit qui et ante hoc Christum et nunc quoque Ecclesiam Christi negavit et, episcopis sanis et integris et viventibus non obtemperans, comitem se et participem morientibus praebuit? Opto vos, fratres charissimi ac desiderantissimi, semper bene valere.
pass_a_gloss: But the lapsed, indeed, knowing the magnitude of their own offense, let them not recede from beseeching the Lord, nor let them abandon the Catholic Church, which is one and alone established by the Lord; but, lingering in satisfactions and beseeching the Lord's mercy, let them knock at the Church, so that they may be received there where they were, and let them return to Christ, from whom they receded. And let them not listen to those who deceive themselves with fallacious and mortal seduction, since it is written: No one deceive you with empty words. For on this account the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Do not be, therefore, partakers of them. Therefore, let no one associate with the disobedient and those not fearing God and totally receding from the Church. But if anyone is impatient at beseeching the Lord who is offended, and does not wish to obey us, but has followed the desperate and the lost, he will impute it to himself when the day of judgment comes. For how will he be able to beseech the Lord on that day, who both before this denied Christ and now also denies the Church of Christ, and, not obeying the healthy and integral and living bishops, has provided himself as a companion and partaker of the dying? I wish you, most dear and most desired brothers, to always be well.

choices.english: No one deceive you with empty words
rejected: Do not let anyone deceive you with empty words

pass_b_english: But the lapsed, knowing the magnitude of their offense, must not stop beseeching the Lord, nor must they abandon the Catholic Church, which is the one and only Church established by the Lord. Instead, they must persevere in making satisfaction and beseeching the Lord's mercy, knocking at the door of the Church, so that they may be received there where they once stood, and return to Christ, from whom they have fallen away (Eph 5:6). They must not listen to those who deceive themselves with a seduction that is both fallacious and mortal, since it is written: 'No one deceive you with empty words.' For on this account the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore, do not become partakers with them. Consequently, let no one associate with the disobedient, those who do not fear God, and those who have totally withdrawn from the Church. But if anyone grows impatient in beseeching the offended Lord and refuses to obey us, choosing instead to follow the desperate and the lost, he will bring the blame upon himself when the day of judgment arrives. For how will he be able to beseech the Lord on that day, he who has both denied Christ before this and now also denies the Church of Christ, and, by refusing to obey bishops who are sound, whole, and still living, has made himself a companion and partner of the dying? I pray, most dear and longed-for brothers, that you may always fare well.

review.notes: Pass B introduces an external scripture citation not present in the Locked Latin: 'from whom they have fallen away (Eph 5:6)'. While the sense of 'recesserunt' aligns with the concept, the instruction forbids adding information not in the source. Additionally, Pass A contains a mistranslation of 'satisfactionibus immorantes' as 'lingering in satisfactions'; the Latin 'immorantes' (from immorari) means 'not delaying' or 'not being idle', whereas 'lingering' implies the opposite of the intended meaning of persevering/not delaying in making satisfaction.
reasons: Pass B adds an external citation '(Eph 5:6)' which is not in the Locked Latin source. Pass A translates 'satisfactionibus immorantes' as 'lingering in satisfactions', which contradicts the Latin 'immorantes' (not delaying/not being idle/not being slothful).
